bug_semantics: ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode in xfixes/disconnect.c does a REQUEST() cast of the client request buffer and then copies stuff->disconnect_mode without REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH. A local X11 client can send a shorter-than-struct SetClientDisconnectMode request so the CARD32 disconnect_mode field is filled from leftover bytes still sitting in the shared request buffer from a previous request, leaking residual request data (CWE-200). The swapped-client SProc only used REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE, which still does not enforce an exact request length. The sibling GetClientDisconnectMode handler in the same file already used REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH, so the missing check is specific to Set.
flaw_origin: The unguarded SetClientDisconnectMode handler was first written when ClientDisconnectMode was added to XFixes (extension v6) as a new file xfixes/disconnect.c. The BIC is the new-file commit that introduced ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode with REQUEST() plus a direct field read and no length check; the immediate parent has neither the file nor the symbol. That first-write survived unchanged on the 21.1 line through xorg-server-21.1.16 until REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH was added.
